title: High‐Contiguity Haplotype‐Resolved Genome Assembly of the Hexaploid Actinidia valvata Rootstock Sheds Light on Waterlogging Resistance Gene
authors:
Miaomiao Lin, 
Zhi Li, 
Cecilia H. Deng, 
Congcong Li, 
Zhengzhen Zhang, 
Yukuo Li, 
Qina Zhang, 
Peng Zhang, 
Leiming Sun, 
Mingyu Liu, 
Jinbao Fang, 
Xiujuan Qi
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 Polyploidisation, creating redundant or diverged copies of the genome, is a major driving force in plant evolution, diversification and environmental adaptation, including for the kiwifruit genus ( Actinidia  Lindl.). We present a high-contiguity, haplotype-resolved genome assembly of the hexaploid  Actinidia valvata  rootstock cultivar ‘Zhongmikangzhen No. 2’ (ZK2), a novel rootstock and the first of its kind to receive Plant Variety Protection in China, exhibiting superior waterlogging tolerance. The assembly, ZK2, contains 174 chromosomes in 6 haplotypes (2 n  = 6 x  = 174), where > 82% of chromosomes per haplotype are telomere-capped at one or both ends, including three haplotypes achieved with 100% telomeric representation. In total, 212 055 protein-coding genes are predicted, or about 35 000 genes per haplotype on average. Our work on comparative genomics, including analyses of TE composition, collinearity, orthologs and phylogenies, strongly reveals an AABBBB subgenome structure derived from ancestral donors  A. polygama  (A1 and A2) and  A. macrosperma  (B1 to B4). Transcriptome analysis showed differential expressions between the homeologs under waterlogging stress, highlighting subgenome-specific regulatory dynamics. A key example involves an ethylene-response factor ( ERF ) gene: when the B1 copy of  ERF  was overexpressed in the kiwifruit transgenic lines, they illustrated an enhanced waterlogging resistance. In addition, this high-quality haplotype-resolved  A. valvata  genome assembly enables functional trait discovery, homeolog-aware genome-wide association studies, and targeted editing of beneficial alleles or homologous gene sets, supporting the breeding of resilient polyploid kiwifruit cultivars and rootstocks. This resource provides a foundation for future research in kiwifruit, particularly for rootstock-mediated crop improvement.

title: The AtMYB2 downstream targets AtMYB48 and AtbHLH68 redundantly regulate cambial cell proliferation and xylem differentiation in Arabidopsis thaliana
authors: Chong Zhang, Xiaorui Guo, Leiqian Sun, Yu Sun, Ziyue Ge, Yawei Fan, Mengyuan Chen, Hui Li, Hai Lu
abstract: This study demonstrates that AtMYB2 negatively regulates cambial cell proliferation and promotes xylem differentiation by directly repressing AtMYB48 and AtbHLH68. Although these two targets function redundantly in xylem development, AtMYB48 preferentially controls secondary cell wall synthesis and programmed cell death, whereas AtbHLH68 predominantly regulates cambial cell proliferation.

title: Pan-orchid transcriptomics sheds light on candidate regulators and the evolution of complex floral morphology and symmetry
authors: Guojin Zhang, Yi Hu, Na Huang, Clancy A. McIntyre, Hong Ma
abstract: This study presents a newly constructed nuclear phylogeny of 709 orchid species and investigates their floral evolution and gene expression, including floral character history, MADS-box gene evolution, and comparative floral organ transcriptomics across four orchid subfamilies. AP3 and AGL6 homologs show conserved lip-preferential expression, and several novel candidate regulatory genes are identified, providing new insights into the evolution of complex floral traits.

title: The GhOFP1–GhTALE–GhXTHB transcriptional cascade regulates vascular cambium development in cotton stems
authors: Jinghui Xu, Linqi Li, Hang Zhao, Xiaohong Liu, Menghan Liu, Peng Wang, Ye Wang, Lisen Liu, Xiaoshuang Zhang, Mengyue Yan, Jingjing Zhan, Xiaoyang Ge
abstract: Vascular cambium proliferation determines radial stem growth and biomass accumulation, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood in cotton. This study identifies a GhOFP1–GhTALE–GhXTHB regulatory module that modulates cambial cell division and radial stem thickening, providing new insights into the molecular control of stem architecture.

title: Plant immune dysregulation disrupts microbe-induced growth promotion and microbiome compatibility
authors: Baoda Han, Anamika Rawat, Sabiha Parween, Waad Alzayed, Huoming Zhang, Rabeaa S. Alkhateeb, Tanja Schmidt, Yao Wu, Carlos Penaloza Rodriguez, Maged M. Saad, Heribert Hirt
abstract: This study reports that the Arabidopsis bik1-1 mutant shows a broad defect in growth promotion by individual beneficial bacterial strains, synthetic communities, and soil-derived microbiomes. This altered response is not caused by loss of BIK1 function but is associated with a chromosomal fragment duplication that increases expression of defense-related genes and causes immune dysregulation in the host. These findings highlight balanced host immune signaling as a key determinant of microbiome compatibility and plant growth outcomes.

title: Streptophyte algae and terrestrialization: breaking down the fundamental challenges from an ECM perspective
abstract: Abstract The successful conquest of land by ancient streptophyte algae is closely related to the structural features and functional roles of their extracellular matrix and associated evolutionary innovations. Terrestrialization 500+ million years ago required adaptation to multiple and novel abiotic and biotic stressors. The establishment of a sessile habit, which encompasses adhesion, likely required special cell surface components like arabinogalactan protein-like macromolecules. The secretion of polysaccharide-rich extracellular polymeric substance provided multiple services, including the establishment of a platform for interactions with surrounding microorganisms (ie, biofilms). Protection against harmful UV radiation likely included production of phenolic compounds, cuticular components, and sporopollenin. Innovations to the various components of the cell wall contributed to the evolution of multicellularity and large thallus sizes, water retention, defense, wound response, and interactions with surrounding microorganisms. Yet we are only in an infancy stage in understanding how specific cell wall components contributed to the invasion of land by streptophyte algae. Future studies are needed that encompass much larger taxonomic screening, detailed glycomics and proteomics, mining of biosynthetic pathways, and comprehensive analyses of cell wall integrity, especially in response to abiotic and biotic stressors of terrestrial habitats.

title: Integrated multi-omics analysis reveals carbon metabolic reprogramming as a mechanism of drought resistance in hybrid rice
authors: Wei Ding, Junguo Bi, Shoujun Chen, Zhen Wu, Zhigang Liao, Lin Huang, Lijun Luo, Liang Chen, Xumin Zhang
abstract: This study demonstrates that the hybrid rice cultivar Hanyou73 achieves drought-resistance heterosis by reprogramming carbon metabolism through a strategic sugar-to-lipid transition regulated by K155 deacetylation of OsPGM3. This metabolic redirection prioritizes local carbon allocation for lipid defenses while preserving systemic carbon export to sustain yield potential, thereby optimizing carbon-use efficiency and mitigating the growth–defense trade-off.

title: An indel in the FAD5 promoter confers cold tolerance by enhancing transcriptional activation of unsaturated fatty acid synthesis in grapevines
authors: Huimin Zhou, Qingyun Li, Darren C.J. Wong, Lin Meng, Yujun Hou, Lina Wang, Yuanxi Kang, Subash Kafle, Yalong Liu, Lei Gao, Meilong Xu, Hailin Shen, Yi Wang, Zhenchang Liang, Qingfeng Wang, Haiping Xin
abstract: This study identifies VaFAD5 as a key gene involved in the cold adaptation of Vitis amurensis. A 6-bp indel in the VaFAD5 promoter confers cold-induced activation by VaDOF17b, leading to increased accumulation of unsaturated fatty acids and enhanced cold tolerance. This favorable genetic variation is prevalent in cold-hardy wild grapevines but largely absent from most cold-sensitive cultivars, providing a promising target for breeding cold-tolerant grapevine varieties.

title: FK506-binding proteins OsFKBP57 and OsFKBP73 confer salt tolerance in rice by activating the SOS pathway while reducing grain protein accumulation through inhibition of BCAT activity
authors: Zhaoyang Dai, Gaoming Chen, Wenwei Zhang, Linglong Liu, Shijun Geng, Xinran Cheng, Wenchao Chi, Jing Li, Chunyuan Wang, Ting Zhu, Xueqian Xie, Shijia Liu, Yunlu Tian, Xi Liu, Xianjun Sun, Hui Zhang, Yan Liu, Zhiguang Sun, Jingfang Li, Baoxiang Wang, Dayong Xu, Chunming Wang, Jianmin Wan
abstract: This study demonstrates that OsFKBP57 and OsFKBP73 confer salt tolerance in rice through the Salt Overly Sensitive (SOS) pathway and simultaneously regulate grain protein content by inhibiting BCAT activity and repressing GluA1-associated glutelin accumulation.

title: LAX PANICLE1 acts as a canonical bHLH transcription factor to regulate inflorescence axillary meristem formation in rice
authors: Debao Fu, Xiaohu Xiong, Minghua Wei, Tian Gao, Tingting Xu, Junkai Zhu, Shuaiguo Ma, Chunmei Zhu, Qiusheng Kong, Changyin Wu
abstract: This study demonstrates that LAX1, a bHLH transcription factor previously thought to lack DNA-binding capacity, possesses intrinsic DNA-binding activity and directly regulates key genes, including OsPID and OsIAA7. By identifying its cognate DNA-binding motif and demonstrating functional conservation across cereal crops, this work establishes a foundation for the use of LAX1 orthologs to improve grain yield.

title: Natural variation in OsbHLH150 confers chilling tolerance in rice by increasing ABA biosynthesis
authors: Jinliang Sun, Xianglan Luo, Xuemei Qin, Ping Gan, Lingwen Meng, Wenshu Liang, Ru Li, Tianmin Ouyang, Weijian Cen, Rongbai Li, Jijing Luo
abstract: This study shows that chilling-induced, OsMAPK3-mediated phosphorylation stabilizes OsbHLH150, which in turn activates OsNCED3 expression and promotes ABA biosynthesis to increase ABA accumulation, ultimately enhancing chilling tolerance in rice. Moreover, introducing OsbHLH150 into chilling-sensitive indica rice significantly enhances chilling tolerance at both the seedling and booting stages.

title: The RLK7–MPK3/6–LEAFY PETIOLE signaling axis mediates growth inhibition during PIP peptide-induced immunity in Arabidopsis
abstract: This study identifies the RLK7–MPK3/6–LEAFY PETIOLE (LEP) signaling axis as a key pathway through which PIP1/2 peptides mediate the trade-off between plant growth and immunity. PIP-induced interaction between RLK7 and SERK coreceptors triggers MPK3/6-dependent phosphorylation events that activate LEP-mediated growth inhibition, whereas loss of LEP function relieves growth inhibition without impairing immune responses. These findings provide a genetic framework for decoupling defense activation from growth inhibition and offer a potential strategy for optimizing crop resilience.

title: A positive feedback loop between NPR1 and SOG1 reinforces genotoxic tolerance in Arabidopsis
abstract: This study demonstrates that the salicylic acid signaling regulator NPR1 and the DNA damage response regulator SOG1 form a positive transcriptional feedback loop that amplifies genotoxic stress responses in Arabidopsis. By cooperatively activating NAC085, the NPR1–SOG1 module enhances tolerance to DNA damage and helps maintain genome integrity under stress conditions.

title: OsFTL1 integrates circadian and photoperiodic signals to optimize flowering time for ecological adaptation in rice
abstract: This study demonstrates that natural variation in the OsFTL1 promoter alters its responsiveness to the circadian oscillator OsCCA1. The OsFTL1 allele from the near-isogenic line NIL(qHD1b), which carries an additional MYB site, confers early flowering without a yield penalty by overcoming Ghd7-mediated repression. These findings reveal a mechanism by which natural promoter variation integrates circadian and photoperiodic signals to optimize rice heading date.

title: The circular RNA circP5CS1 coordinates plant immunity by sequestering miR167 to modulate ARF6/8 signaling and repressing P5CS1-mediated proline biosynthesis in Arabidopsis
abstract: This study demonstrates that circP5CS1 functions as a regulatory hub linking miR167 signaling, proline metabolism, and immunity in Arabidopsis. Mechanistically, circP5CS1 sequesters miR167a/b to modulate ARF6/8 signaling while repressing the expression of its host gene, P5CS1, thereby coordinating hormone-associated defense responses and proline biosynthesis during pathogen infection.

title: Antagonistic chromatin regulation of LHY homologs by GmASH2R and GmNF-YC4 fine-tunes soybean flowering time for latitudinal adaptation
abstract: This study reports that a COMPASS-like epigenetic complex containing GmASH2R1 and GmASH2R2 promotes soybean flowering by enhancing H3K4me3 deposition at GmLHYs and activating their expression, while two NF-Y transcription factors, GmNF-YC4a and GmNF-YC4b, antagonize this activation, thereby fine-tuning flowering time for latitudinal adaptation.

title: Gene Editing of Nicotiana benthamiana Architecture for Space‐Efficient Production of Recombinant Proteins in Closed Environments
authors:
Béatrice Giroux, 
Kristina LeBreux, 
Louis Feyzeau, 
Marie‐Claire Goulet, 
Charles Goulet, 
Dominique Michaud
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 Indoor vertical farming (VF) offers practical advantages for the cultivation of plant protein bio-factories including plant uniformity, product consistency, water/nutrient recycling and production cycles on a year-round basis. Much progress has been achieved toward the development of innovative systems for artificial lighting, automated irrigation, plant handling, environmental control and space use optimization in VF systems. Here, we used a CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing approach to generate mutant lines of protein expression host  Nicotiana benthamiana  presenting a compact, space-efficient phenotype suited to VF systems. Our strategy consisted of altering apical dominance by suppressing the synthesis of strigolactone, a negative regulator of axillary bud outgrowth. Strigolactone-depleted lines were generated by hindering the expression of either  Carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 7  (CCD7) or  Carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 8  (CCD8), two key enzymes of the strigolactone synthetic pathway. Knocking out of either enzyme had no impact on the plant's growth rate but drastically influenced its auxin/cytokinin ratio, leaf proteome and overall architecture. The ΔCCD mutants exhibited an axillary growth-oriented development pattern, altered glycolytic and malate-processing metabolic fluxes to drive pyruvate and cytokinin production, and a spatial footprint reduced by 45%–50% compared to the LAB strain commonly used for protein expression. Most importantly, recombinant protein yields per plant were maintained in the mutant lines, as illustrated with GFP and rituximab, a chimeric antibody of therapeutic value. Our data confirm the usefulness of ΔCCD7 and ΔCCD8 knockouts leading to strigolactone depletion for the generation of compact, space-efficient  N. benthamiana  lines better suited to VF systems.

title: Two transcription factors, MYB64 and MYB119, and their target cis-regulatory element control egg cell-specific gene expression in Arabidopsis
abstract: This study identifies a cis-regulatory element, ESM, within the ECS1 promoter that is required for egg cell-specific expression. The ESM motif is evolutionarily conserved in the promoters of multiple egg cell-specific genes. The authors further demonstrate that the transcription factors MYB64 and MYB119 directly bind to the ESM element and cooperatively activate egg cell-specific gene expression.

title: The SPL transcription factor OsSPL10 regulates rice tillering through auxin signaling to maintain grain yield under drought stress
abstract: This study demonstrates that the transcription factor OsSPL10 regulates rice tillering and yield through the auxin signaling pathway. The authors identify OsSPL10T-Hap1 as a favorable natural allele associated with increased tiller number and enhanced drought tolerance. Furthermore, genome editing of OsSPL10 improves rice yield under both normal and drought conditions, highlighting its potential as a valuable target for breeding high-yielding, drought-resilient rice cultivars.

title: Allelic variation in the thioredoxin TRX-M4 influences carbon partitioning to control soluble sugar content in apple fruit
abstract: This study identifies a naturally occurring coding SNP in the apple thioredoxin gene TRX-M4 through QTL mapping and demonstrates its role in regulating carbon partitioning during fruit maturation. The two TRX-M4 alleles differ in their capacity to promote ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase and starch synthase 1 activities, thereby influencing the allocation of carbon between starch and soluble sugars and ultimately determining apple fruit sweetness.
